Content

Sources

  • Kautilya's Arthashastra: He was contemporary to Chandragupta Maurya. Arthashastra describes the administration and state policies of Mauryan Empire during Chandragupta Maurya's time.
  • Vishakadutta's Mudrarakshasa: It is a Sanskrit play that narrates the ascent of emperor Chandragupta Maurya to power in India. This play describes them as belonging to a lower caste.
  • Indica written by Megasthenes: It includes all the detailed account of how things were run in Mauryan Empire.
  • Buddhist Literature: Jataka tales, Dipavamsa / Mahavamsa, Divyadana.

MAURYA DYNASTY

Chandragupta Maurya (322 BC-298 BC)

  • He was the founder of Mauryan Dynasty and ascended the throne by defeating the last ruler of Nanda Dynasty → Dhanananda, with the help of Kautilya (also known as Chanakya / Vishnugupta) in 322 BCE.
  • He defeated Seleucus Nicator (Frontier of Alexander The Great).
  • Son: Bindusara
  • He built a department "Kosthagara": For storage of grains (mentioned in Sohgaura Copper Plate inscription).

About Seleucus Nicator

  • Seleucus Nicator founded Seleucid Dynasty (member of Macedonian Greek Dynasty) ruling in Northwestern parts of the Indian subcontinent.
  • Megasthenes was sent as an ambassador by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra (corrected: Megasthenes served in Chandragupta's court, not Seleucus's).
  • Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus Nicator and was married to his daughter Helena.

Bindusara (297 BC-273 BC)

  • He is also known as "Amitrochates" by the Greek.
  • He asked for sweet wine, dry figs and a philosopher from Antiochus I of Syria.
  • He is known for conquering the land between the two seas.
  • He patronised Ajivikas.
  • He was visited by Greek ambassador → Deimachus.
  • Son: Ashoka

Ashoka (268 BC-232 BC)

  • Ashoka ascended the throne with the help of Radhagupta (Minister).
  • He fought Kalinga War (261 BCE) 8 years after his coronation.
  • He replaced Bherighosha (sound of war) with Dhammaghosha (sound of dhamma/righteousness) after the Kalinga War.
  • He sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra to Ceylon (now known as Sri Lanka) to spread Buddhism.

Ashokan Edict

  • Edicts of Ashoka are found in Rocks and Pillars.
  • Rock Edicts: There are 14 Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka meaning a maximum of 14 lines are engraved in Rocks.

William Jones (founder of Asiatic Society of Bengal, 1784) was also involved in deciphering of major Ashokan Rock Edicts.

James Princep was the 1st to decipher Ashokan inscriptions in 1837.

Major Rock Edicts

  • Total: 14
  • Total languages: 3
  • Total scripts used: 4
  • Most inscriptions were in: Prakrit language in Brahmi script
  • Script used in Afghanistan: Greek and Aramaic
  • Script used in Northwestern parts of India: Kharosthi
  • In inscriptions he is mentioned as: Devanami Piyadassi (Meaning: Devon ka Priya → Beloved of God)

10 Places where Ashokan Rock Edicts have been Found

  1. 1. Kandahar Bilingual Inscription → Kandahar, Afghanistan
  2. 2. Shahbazgarhi in Kharoshthi script → Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
  3. 3. Mansehra Rock Edicts → Mansehra, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan
  4. 4. Kalsi → Dehradun, Uttarakhand
  5. 5. Girnar → Gujarat (14 lines are inscribed in Girnar major Rock Edicts)
  6. 6. Sopara → Maharashtra
  7. 7. Dhauli → Bhubaneshwar, Odisha
  8. 8. Jaugada → Odisha
  9. 9. Sannati → Karnataka
  10. 10. Yerragudi → Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh

Map 1: Ashoka's Rock Edicts

14th Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka

EdictSubject
**Edict 1Prohibits animal slaughter. Ban festive gatherings and the killing of animals. Only two peacocks and one deer were killed in Ashoka's kitchen. He wished to discontinue this practice also.
Edict 2Providing care for man and animals describes Chola, Pandya, kingdoms of south India.
Edict 3Generosity to Brahmans.
**Edict 4Dhammaghosha (sound of dhamma) over Bherighosha (sound of war).
Edict 5Concerns over policy towards slaves.
Edict 6Welfare measures.
**Edict 7Requests tolerance for all religions.
Edict 8Describes Ashoka's first Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya and Bodhi tree.
Edict 9Condemns popular ceremonies. Stress on ceremonies of dhamma.
Edict 10Condemns the desire for fame and glory. It stresses the popularity of Dhamma.
Edict 11Elaborates dhamma.
**Edict 12Directed and determined requests for tolerance among different religious sects.
**Edict 13Ashoka's victory over Kalinga.
Edict 14Describes engraving of inscriptions in different parts of the country.

  • Edict XIII (13): Kalinga War (Kalinga was the ancient name of Odisha).

Minor Rock Edicts

  • Four Edicts where Ashoka has been mentioned by his name.
  • These four are:
  • Maski → Karnataka
  • Nettur → Andhra Pradesh
  • Brahmagiri → Karnataka
  • Gujarra → Madhya Pradesh

Pillar Edicts

  • Total: 7 (meaning: 7 lines)

Delhi Topra Pillar Edict

  • It comprises all the 7 Ashokan Pillar Edicts and only the 7th Edict is considered as the longest amongst them all.
  • Only one language (Prakrit) and only one script (Brahmi) is used.
  • Delhi Topra Pillar was transferred from Haryana to in Delhi by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
  • Lauriya Areraj
  • Lauriya Nandangarh — Both in Bihar
  • Barabar Hill Caves in Bihar → Built by Ashoka for Buddhist monks.
  • Lomas Rishi Caves in Bihar.
  • Nagarjunt Caves in Bihar → Built by Dasrath Maurya (grandson of Ashoka).
  • Konagamana / Kanakamuni Stupa → Rebuilt by Ashoka (after he visited Nigali Sagar).

Inscriptions

  • It depicts that Ashoka traveled to the Buddha's birthplace. He reduced the taxes of the people living in that area.
  • The last ruler of Mauryan Dynasty: Brihadratha (who was defeated by Pushyamitra Shunga).

Mauryan Administration

  • Saptanga Theory by Kautilya: He mentioned 7 elements to rule an administration effectively.
  1. 1. King: Raja
  2. 2. Secretary: Amatya
  3. 3. Territory: Janpada
  4. 4. Fort: Durga
  5. 5. Treasury: Kosha
  6. 6. Army: Danda
  7. 7. Friend: Mitra

Five Provinces under Mauryan Administration

ProvinceCapital
Prachyapatha (East)Tosali
Avantipatha (West)Ujjain
Uttarapatha (North)Taxila
Dakshinapatha (South)Suvarnagiri
Prachi (At present: UP + Bihar)Patliputra

Tax System

  • Tax paid in gold: Hiranya
  • Emergency tax: Pranaya
  • Taxes paid in kind by villages: Pindakara
  • Army maintenance tax: Senabhaktam
  • Extra tax: Parsvam

Two Types of Courts

  1. 1. Dharmasthiya Nyayalaya: Presided by Vyavaharika (personal disputes)
  2. 2. Kantakasodhana Nyayalaya: Presided by Pradeshta (disputes between state and people).
  • It was adopted as the National Emblem on 24th Jan 1950 and it shows Dhammaparivartan of Ashoka.
  • Here, Ashoka commemorated the first Sermon of Buddha.
  • Animals: Lion, Elephants, Horse, Bull

Officers

  • Sannidhata: Chief treasury officer (CTO)
  • Samaharta: Collector general of revenue
  • Gopa: Responsible for account
  • Akshapatalik: Accountant General / Audit Officer
  • Nagaraka: Responsible for city administration
  • Sitadhyaksha: Superintendent of Agriculture
  • Samsthadhyaksha: Responsible for market
  • Navadhyaksha: Superintendent of ships
  • Ashvadhyaksha: Commanding officer of the cavalry (Ghode wali fauj)
  • Shulkadhyaksha: Superintendent of Toll Tax
  • Dhamma Mahamatta: New post created by Ashoka to check if people are following the concepts of Dhamma

According to Megasthenes, administration consisted of (as mentioned in Indica):

  • Municipal administration of 6 committees with 5 members each.
  • Army of 6 Committee with 5 member each.
  • Kautilya proposes a seven-part structure for the state including the king, ministers, territory, forts, treasury, military, and allies (also known as Saptanga theory).

According to Arthashastra

  • Women occupied a high position in society and were a part of Army.

Ports

  • West: Bharuch, Sopara
  • East: Tamralipti (Bengal)

Provincial Administration

Society

  • Society was divided into 4 varnas.
  • Society was divided into 7 classes, as described by Megasthenes in "Indica". They were divided into:
TRICK (PCS TWO C)
1.Philosophers→P
2.Cultivators / Farmers→C
3.Hunters and Shepherd→S
4.Traders→T
5.Warrior→W
6.Overseer (spy)→O
7.Councillor→C
  • Antyaja: Without any caste
  • 8 types of marriages were mentioned and divorce was allowed.

Megasthenes described Pataliputra as a large and beautiful city, surrounded by a massive wall. The city had 570 towers and 64 gates, showcasing its grandeur and strategic importance.
